title: The spawn-lead workflow
description: One unit of work gets one Herdr workspace, one Git worktree and one lead agent. You talk only to the lead; the lead delegates.

props.body: All workers share one worktree, so two workers editing the same file will collide. The skill's only guard is a rule: give concurrent agents different files, and only the lead commits. Nothing enforces either rule. The workflow also needs `HERDR_ENV=1`; outside Herdr it stops. The skill was added in the latest agents2 work (commit d163bd6) and the text here is its first version.
props.title: Open risks first
The point
props.deck: A lead agent plans, delegates, reviews and integrates. Workers and subagents do the typing, all inside the lead's worktree.

props.content: Terms: the **lead** is the Pi agent in tab 1. A **worker** is a Herdr agent in its own tab. A **subagent** is a background Pi agent started with the `Agent` tool. The **shared worktree** is the lead's worktree, used by everyone.

props.title: Creating the lead
props.caption: Seven commands in order; reuse an existing worktree for the same purpose instead.
steps: c -> h : herdr worktree list, check for reuse
c -> h : herdr worktree create --branch name --path ~/dev/worktrees/repo/name
c -> h : herdr agent start name-lead --kind pi
h -> l : Pi starts in the root pane
c -> l : herdr agent prompt with the brief
note over c, l: caller reports label, path, branch; does not focus

props.title: The rules that keep it safe
props.deck: The lead edits no code and runs no long jobs.

rows.title: One writer to git
rows.body: Only the lead commits. Workers leave changes uncommitted.

rows.title: Disjoint files
rows.body: Concurrent agents touch different files. Same files means run them in sequence.

rows.title: Verify last
rows.body: The lead runs full checks after integrating, never while a worker is editing.

rows.title: Ask first
rows.body: Pushing, opening PRs or any external action needs the user's approval. Teardown only on request, and no --force on dirty work without approval.

routing.when: One-off, self-contained: research, review, a quick check
Ongoing or multi-step work the user may steer or follow up
routing.how: Own tab in the shared worktree
